summary.text: Russell Black is a Republican state senator from Maine, representing Senate District 5, who is running for the Maine House of Representatives, District 74, in the November 3, 2026 general election. A farmer and logger, he served in the Maine House from 2010 to 2018 before moving to the Senate.

paragraphs.text: Russell Black lives in Wilton, Maine, and graduated from Mt. Blue High School.
His career experience includes owning Black Acres Farm and working as a farmer and logger.
Ballotpedia lists service as director and president of the Wilton Lions Club, director and vice president of the Franklin County Farm Bureau, and director of the Farmington Farmers Union.

Black represented District 114 in the Maine House of Representatives from 2010 to 2018, where he served on the Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry Committee, and then joined the Maine State Senate in 2018.
His current Senate term ends on December 1, 2026, and he is not running for re-election to the Senate.
He advanced from the June 9, 2026 Republican primary for House District 74 and faces Democrat Marc Edwards in the general election.
In the 2025-2026 session he was assigned to the Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry Committee and the Senatorial Vote Committee.
